newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian business confidence still falling - NAB.
newsitem.headline: Australian business confidence still falling - NAB.

text.p: Recent falls in Australian interest rates have failed to arrest a decline in business confidence, the National Australia Bank (NAB) business survey for May has found.
Conditions across sectors remain varied, and a generalised pick up in activity is yet to occur with underlying annual growth remaining at around 2.5 to 3.0 percent, the NAB said.
The survey also found that the labour market remained weak. Against that, wage pressures eased in May and price pressures remained subdued.
The NAB's index of business confidence eased to 9.2 points in May from a level of 124 points in April and 14.0 points for the March quarter.
The composite index of business conditions remained at negative five points in both May and April, down from a March quarter reading of negative four points.
"Services continue to perfrom relatively well, but manufacturing, wholesaling and, to a lesser extent, retailing continue to report poor conditions," the NAB survey found.
"Mining also reported poor conditions in May for the first time since late 1995," the report said.
While trading conditions had improved slightly since the March quarter, this improvement was offset by further falls in profitability and employment.
NAB said that based on the historical trend its employment index suggested recent official data may have understated recent employment growth.
"That said, the poor outcomes recorded by our survey in May and April, at the very least, points to a still fundamentally weak labour market," the survey said.
Firms reported their first rundown in stocks since mid 1993, with the rundown evident in most sectors except mining.
Forward orders were steady in May after a small fall in April.
Reflecting still subdued trading conditions, the survey's measure of capacity utilisation in May was unchanged from the March quarter reading of 79.9 percent.
The NAB survey found prices rose only 0.04 percent in May, following rises of 0.02 percent in April and 0.12 percent in March.
"Margins in the retail remained under downward pressure, implying little increase in the underlying CPI (consumer price index) over the past few months," NAB said.
As well, the NAB's measure of labour cost growth decreased significantly to 0.22 percent in May from 0.39 percent in April, with wage pressures easing in all sectors except construction.
